# HR Automation — rebuild

The ground-up rebuild of UCSD's UCPath HR automation. This repository is **not** production. The
legacy repository at `/Users/julianhein/Projects/hr-automation` runs every real HR transaction and
stays the sole production authority until a single all-at-once cutover (D89/D93).

Current status is owned by the plan, not by this file: `npm run cli -- phase` prints the runtime's
`completedThrough`/`active`, and the phase docs `docs/rebuild/00`–`06` record what each phase landed,
what it found, and what left it by explicit disposition (Phases 1–2 complete 2026-08-04/2026-08-09).

## Before you start

**The plan is the SSOT — read it, do not re-derive it.** It has three parts: the **tree** at
`docs/roadmap/roadmap.md` (the machine-readable plan + the site's source + the governance rules), the
**phase docs** `docs/rebuild/00`–`06` (actionable: one per phase, the number IS the phase), and the
**specs** in `docs/rebuild/reference/` (not actionable; cited by slug).

- `docs/roadmap/roadmap.md` — the plan as written, in the roadmap notation (headings = nodes,
  `builds:`/`needs:`/`doc:` lines); `docs/roadmap/index.html` is GENERATED from it by
  `npm run roadmap`. After `roadmap:end` its **Governance** section owns the one-plan rule, the D1
  ownership map and D263.
- The **phase docs** under `docs/rebuild/` — tasks, what is done and what is left, exit criteria, and
  the decisions that phase ratified. `00-design-the-foundation` · `01-build-the-spine` ·
  `02-prove-writes-build-the-tails` · `03a-finish-the-dashboard` · `03b-finish-separations` ·
  `03c-migrate-the-remaining-workflows` · `03d-co-operate-with-Codex` · `04-close-the-deferrals` ·
  `05-cut-over` · `06-ship-the-desktop-app`. Phase 3 is four docs (3a/3b/3c/3d); in prose
  **`doc NN`** means one of these.
- `docs/rebuild/reference/decisions.md` — the decision changelog (D1–D264; **D131 is a retired gap —
  never reuse it**). A **pointer index**, not a spec: it tells you which doc owns a contract. Never
  implement from it.
- `docs/rebuild/reference/` — the contracts, each doc owning its own; in prose **`ref <slug>`**:
  `charter` (the operator's vision + the non-negotiables) · `task-contract` (tasks, stores, drivers) ·
  `workflow-model` (the builder, descriptors, the run state machine) · `dashboard-surfaces` (spans,
  the ONE projection, every surface) · `execution-and-sessions` (workers, queues, browser sessions) ·
  `data-intake-and-edit-data` (extraction, OCR, intake, Edit Data) · `write-safety` (the write
  sequencer, intents, the ALWAYS-GATE) · `guards-and-tests` (the guard/test architecture) ·
  `clock-config-secrets` (clock, config resolver, secrets) · `operator-trust` (failures, receipts,
  knowledge, the explorer) · `frontend-backend-integration` (the BFF, the wire, the parity lane) ·
  `foundation-gap-audit` (frozen — a design input, owns nothing) · `stores` (the DERIVED store
  catalog — read it before authoring a task, and remember the code wins over it).
- `docs/rebuild/reference/lessons.md` — the dated lessons ledger (`ref lessons`): 60 entries of
  "X looked safe and did Y", each naming its decision. Read it before kernel / driver / dashboard /
  write-safety work; add new root-level lessons THERE (module lessons stay in the module's AGENTS.md).
- `docs/rebuild/00`–`06` — the ACTIONABLE plan: one doc per phase, the number IS the phase
  (`03a`/`03b`/`03c` are phase 3). Each owns its phase's tasks, its "Decisions this phase ratified"
  and its **exit criteria**; `docs/roadmap/roadmap.md` is the summary (the tree + the governance
  prose + the phases at a glance). The old `07-master-plan.md` was dissolved into them on
  2026-08-20 and is preserved, with a section-by-section table of where everything went, at
  `docs/rebuild/history/superseded/2026-08-20-master-plan-dissolved.md`.
- `docs/rebuild/guard-inventory.json` — the reviewed guard manifest. `tests/unit/architecture/`
  must match it exactly, both directions.
- `docs/rebuild/history/` — history, organized by kind (`doc-reviews/`, `design-inputs/`,
  `superseded/`) and indexed by its own `README.md`. Superseded by the owning docs wherever they
  differ; never cite as normative.

**A decision is not ratified until it lands in its owning doc, in the same commit that records it.**
`reference/decisions.md` gets a one-line pointer; the owner gets the normative text.

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck          # tsc --noEmit over src/, tests/, scripts/ — one program, no exclusions
npm run lint               # eslint src tests scripts --max-warnings 0 — zero-debt, no manifest
npm run test               # every vitest project (unit + architecture)
npm run test:architecture  # the guard suite alone
npm run test:coverage      # 60/80 lines/statements/functions floors + the suite-size report
npm run test:watch

npm run test:parity        # ref frontend-backend-integration §7 visual/a11y parity lane — builds the bundle, ASSERTS every reference
npm run test:parity:update # the ONE deliberate way to re-freeze a reference (PARITY_UPDATE=1)

npm run cli               # the runtime CLI (help | phase | dashboard | worker | dry-run-scenario | explain | storage | ocr)
npm run cli -- dry-run-scenario <workflow> --subject <label> # execute exactly one T1b manifest case
npm run dashboard         # the dev dashboard in ONE terminal: BFF (3938) + vite (5174); Ctrl+C stops both
npm run cli -- dashboard  # the BFF alone (dashboard:prod — see D189, the prod mode is unbuilt)
npm run web               # the vite dev server alone, proxying /api to a BFF you started yourself
npm run web:build         # production bundle into dist/dashboard (test:parity builds this itself)

npm run build:manifest     # regenerate src/domain/workflow/generated-build-manifest.ts
npm run roadmap            # render docs/roadmap/index.html from docs/roadmap/roadmap.md (the plan, in the roadmap notation)
npm run roadmap:check      # fail if the committed site is stale
```

`build:manifest` recomputes every descriptor's `contractFingerprint` from its source closure. Run it
after ANY edit under a descriptor's import closure (which includes `src/base/**` and most of
`src/domain/**`) — `descriptor-coverage` regenerates and fails on a diff, so a stale manifest is a
red gate, not a silent drift.

The gate family is deliberately plain (`typecheck`/`lint`/`test:coverage`, D191 — `test:coverage` is
a strict superset of the earlier `test`+`test:architecture` pair and measured faster); the old
`*:rebuild` names retired with D93 and the `rebuild:` runtime prefix with D247 (2026-08-20) — this is
its own repository, so its commands are plain `cli` / `dashboard` / `web`. See "Operational
isolation" below for what still MUST differ from the legacy checkout.

## Fail loud — no unverified silent fallbacks

**The system this replaces submits REAL HR transactions. Correctness beats graceful degradation
every time.** A fallback that silently substitutes a plausible-but-wrong value when something fails
is the single most dangerous pattern here — it hides the failure and can push wrong data (wrong pay
rate, wrong person, wrong department, a blank or duplicate document, a false "submitted") into a
live UCPath / Kuali / Kronos / OnBase / I-9 transaction, or mislead the operator into acting on a
lie. When it fails silently we never find out; when it fails loud we fix it.

**The rule:** when an operation fails or an expected value is missing, do **NOT** substitute a
default, an alternative selector or element, a cached-or-"latest" value, a fabricated constant, a
"safe" guess, or a swallowed-error return, and then continue as if nothing happened. **Throw with a
legible message naming the offending value / EID / field**, so the error surfaces and gets corrected
at the source.

**A fallback is acceptable only when BOTH hold:**

1. The fallback path is itself **verified correct** for the exact case it handles (live-verified for
   selectors and page state; test-pinned for pure logic) — and its verification is recorded (a
   `// verified <date>` comment, a lesson, or a test), AND
2. Absence, or the fallback case, is a **genuinely valid expected state** (e.g. "no search results"
   is a real outcome; a documented default that is provably right).

If you cannot satisfy both, **fail loud**. When in doubt, throw.

**Not a fallback (these are fine):** retrying the _same_ operation on a transient error — that
re-runs the operation, it does not substitute data. Swallowing an error is fine only when the
_action itself_ is genuinely optional AND the caller does not treat the result as load-bearing.

**When you catch, don't swallow:** a `catch` that returns a default / empty / `{}` / `null` / `0` /
`true` and lets execution continue must instead re-throw (or at minimum log AND propagate a
distinguishable "unknown" the caller checks). Never let "the check failed" become indistinguishable
from "the check passed / found nothing." `catch { won = true }`, `catch { return [] }`,
`JSON.parse(...) catch { return {} }`, `.catch(() => ({ match: true }))`, and `?? "queued"` on
corrupted input are bugs, not resilience.

This tree is zero-debt from its first file: `npm run lint` carries `--max-warnings 0` and there is
no debt manifest. The mechanical arms live in `tests/unit/architecture/helpers/ratchet-arms.ts`
(fail-loud-catch-default, nullish-literal-data-fallback, wait-for-timeout, inline selectors,
evaluate-named-fn, import cycles, layer matrix, code conventions, tailwind palette), each executed
against a violating fixture by `guard-manifest.test.ts` so a dead arm cannot stand in for
enforcement.

## Cross-repo rules (D93/D94)

**The legacy repo is a frozen production reference, not a dependency.**s

- **Never import, invoke, proxy, or read the legacy repo's live state from `src/`.** Two
  repositories share no module graph — this is now structural, not merely banned. The only code
  permitted to reach across is the **guard lane**, which audits legacy as data.
- **Porting = copy with provenance.** When you bring verified knowledge across (a selector, a
  parsing rule, a page-state fact), copy it and record **the legacy commit hash and source path** in
  the ported code. Never link it at runtime — which is impossible anyway.
- **Legacy change accounting is RETIRED (D150, 2026-08-05).** The two repositories no longer touch
  each other in either direction: nothing here reads legacy's working tree, and legacy work never
  blocks a rebuild gate. `config/legacy-change-accounting.json` is a frozen historical record of
  what was reconciled through the split — do not extend it. **What replaced it:** the risk was a
  ported selector or page-state fact going stale after legacy fixed it, and that is now covered by
  **live re-verification at each workflow's migration**, which the charter already makes mandatory
  and pre-authorized. A selector checked against the live system beats one diffed against legacy's
  copy of it. `legacy-selector-port-provenance` is unaffected: it pins all 406 keys to a FIXED
  legacy commit's blobs, so legacy moving on cannot invalidate it.
- **Nothing in the legacy repo may be deleted** during the rebuild or the initial cutover. The whole
  repository is the D89 rollback asset.
- The guard lane finds the legacy repo at `../hr-automation`, overridable with
  `HRAUTO_LEGACY_REPO`. It **fails loud** when the repo is missing — a skipped legacy audit is
  exactly the drift D93 warns about.
- Inventories that span both repos (`src/domain/runtime-environment.ts`) mark legacy paths with an
  explicit **`legacy:` scheme**. Both repos have a `src/` — `src/cli.ts` exists in both — so a bare
  path is ambiguous. Unprefixed always means this repo.

## Operational isolation

A repository boundary does not separate two runtimes on **one machine**. `config/runtime-isolation.json`
pins what must differ, and `operational-isolation.test.ts` proves it:

|                           | legacy                                           | rebuild                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| state root                | `.tracker`                                       | `.tracker-rebuild`                                           |
| artifact root             | `.tracker`                                       | `.tracker-rebuild/artifacts`                                 |
| backend / frontend port   | 3838 / 5173                                      | 3938 / 5174                                                  |
| process locks             | `.tracker/daemons`                               | `.tracker-rebuild/locks`                                     |
| browser profile / session | `.auth` / `hrauto-legacy`                        | `.auth` / `hrauto-rebuild` (D216 — roots are repo-relative and never collide; the SESSION namespace is the distinct half) |
| launch commands           | `dashboard`, `dashboard:prod`, `dashboard:watch` | `dashboard`, `dashboard:prod`, `cli` (D247 — names may coincide; each must be byte-exactly its declared script) |

Command NAMES are not an isolation resource (D247): a muscle-memory `npm run dashboard` in the wrong
checkout starts that checkout's dashboard on its own port under its own roots and locks, which the
rows above make legible and harmless. Isolation values reach the runtime through one
exported direct-`const` `defineRuntimeIsolation` call that a composition root invokes at top level —
an identifier mention, or a call inside an uninvoked function, is not proof.

## Live verification — standing pre-authorization (always available, never ask)

**The live environment is always available, and reaching it for verification is pre-authorized.
Never ask whether live access is up, whether to spend the live session, or to confirm a Duo prompt —
assume yes and proceed.** This covers the whole range: a read-only selector `snapshot`, a login smoke
check, a live collector, and a full live workflow dry-run against real UCPath / CRM / Kuali /
ServiceNow / I-9. Duo is cleared hands-off by Duo Autopilot on every verification path, so there is
no phone-approval step and nothing to sign off. The safety boundary for a live _workflow_ run is
`dryRun=true` (no UCPath transaction, no Kuali finalization) — that, not gated access, is what keeps
a live run safe. If one system is genuinely down, skip it and proceed with the rest.

Mapping or verifying a selector is **pre-approved** — do it whenever a fix or debugging needs it, and
never pause to ask. A `snapshot` is a read-only view of a page; treat it like running a test.

`playwright-cli` runs **headless by default**. The loop is: open headless → `snapshot` → read the ref
ids → confirm or repair the locator.

```bash
playwright-cli -s=sel open "<url>"          # headless — just omit --headed
playwright-cli -s=sel snapshot              # accessibility tree + ref ids
playwright-cli --raw snapshot > /tmp/s.yml  # grep-friendly dump for big pages
playwright-cli -s=sel close
```

**Auth-gated pages (UCPath/PeopleSoft, CRM, Kuali, ServiceNow, I-9) — use Duo Autopilot.** The
`duo-autopilot/` extension answers the Duo MFA WebAuthn ceremony itself, so an auth-gated login runs
unattended. You still fill the SSO username/password from `.env`
(`UCPATH_USER_ID` / `UCPATH_PASSWORD`). It needs Playwright's **full** bundled Chromium
(`channel: chromium`) — the lightweight headless shell cannot load extensions. See
`duo-autopilot/README.md`. The one thing it cannot do unattended is a brand-new credential
enrollment.

**Always** `close` the session when done and sweep orphans (`playwright-cli list` →
`playwright-cli close-all`) — these are real Chromium processes.

Until this repo grows its own driver layer, live _selector_ work still happens against the legacy
repo's registry; port what you verify with provenance (see cross-repo rules above).

## Environment

`.env` is gitignored and NOT part of the repo. Copy `.env.example` and fill it, or copy the legacy
repo's `.env`. `src/domain/config/resolve.ts` implements `env > settings.json > default` exactly
once; `src/domain/secrets.ts` is the **only** module permitted to read a credential from
`process.env` (`secrets-single-source.test.ts` enforces it). A credential must never be interpolated
into a message — `no-secret-values-in-logs.test.ts` enforces that half.

Dry-run subjects live in the strict, recursively frozen `config/test-subjects.json` registry. A
scenario asks for a label; the loader requires that label's workflow and kind to match its manifest.
`gone` / `unknown` / `consumed` labels resolve `blocked` before any browser starts. An `available`
entry that cannot form the workflow's exact canonical input is a registry defect and throws with the
label and `lastObserved` date. Commit every known non-sensitive input field; real EIDs stay in `.env`
behind the closed EID references read only by `src/domain/secrets.ts`.

> 2026-08-25 — A named canary looked like reusable fixture data, but two earlier Kuali actions had
> already disappeared between live passes and the current finalization canary still lacked a real
> transaction number before 2026-08-28. Availability without a dated observation turns normal live
> subject decay into misleading test red; availability with incomplete input is instead a named
> registry defect.

## Conventions

- **Archived capture resources (DCA4):** `queries/archive.ts` binds resource status and downloads
  to the exact archived run, verifies its immutable content digest, and resolves byte metadata only
  from its frozen capture tiles. Repeated tile ids must agree on the complete byte reference.
  Status uses the shared verify-only stream; downloads independently materialize verified bytes.
  Never consult current runs/indexes/descriptors or infer a purge from a retention deadline. The
  two archive resource routes in `routes/api.ts` report named, path-free archive failures and keep
  downloads no-store, nosniff and attachment-only; resource URLs bind both ids in the strict wire.
- **2026-08-28 — operator skills and internal playbooks are separate surfaces.** The repository's
  operator commands are `hr-manage`, `hr-scan`, `hr-workflow`, and `hr-lesson`. Codex stores
  repo-specific helper guidance under `.agents/skill-library/<name>/REFERENCE.md`; Claude may keep a
  model-visible helper under `.claude/skills/` only with `user-invocable: false`. `hr-debug` is a
  helper reached through the global `debug` router, and workflow resources generated by
  `hr-workflow` are reached through `hr-manage`; neither adds another operator command. Marketplace
  caches are dependencies, never edited as user-owned skills.
- **2026-08-27 — supervised delegation must prove its native role.** Codex supervised tasks use only
  `sup_scout`, `sup_analyst`, `sup_luna`, `sup_terra`, or `sup_sol`; pass the exact native
  `agent_type` and begin `task_name` with that same role. Claude uses only its native `sup-scout` / `sup-analyst` research
  roles and `sup-sonnet` / `sup-opus` / `sup-fable` execution roles, with the role at the start of the
  visible description. Never substitute a generic/default/worker/explorer agent or a bare model
  override. If the required role is unavailable, fail loud instead of silently downgrading it. A
  new coordinator owns `docs/coordinator/<task>/` for every task-scoped coordination artifact:
  `project-profile.md`, board, run plan, briefs, research, reports, decisions, evidence, and partial
  handoffs. The profile records this repository's plan authorities (`docs/roadmap/roadmap.md` and the
  active `docs/rebuild/` phase docs), owning references/decisions, gates, permissions, and the
  worktree + `feature/<unit>` + `--no-ff` integration rules above. Product code, tests, fixtures, and
  canonical docs stay in their owning paths. Prompts supply the exact profile/workspace paths and one
  unique artifact path per writer; parallel workers use that relative path in their own worktrees,
  while read-only agents return findings for the supervisor to persist. Existing coordination files
  stay at established paths unless the operator requests migration. Board writes still require the
  exact absolute path and explicit close-out authorization. Once every run closes, the coordinator
  reconciles verified outcomes into only the necessary roadmap, rebuild/phase plan, owning
  spec/decision, and applicable `AGENTS.md`, commits those updates, and closes the board with
  pointers. The workspace is retained unless the operator explicitly requests archival or removal;
  successful close never auto-handoffs. A coordinator enters stateless discussion or grilling only
  when explicitly asked and writes none of it until the operator says to record it.
- `src/workflows/` has exactly two folder kinds (D265/D266): a top-level folder is a rail workflow,
  and a child folder is one declared timeline step. A chunk harness lives in the matching step
  folder with role `{ kind: "chunk-harness", of, step }`; it remains independently startable,
  nests under its composition in the picker/Explorer, and never appears in the rail. There is no
  `src/workflows/proving/` and no registered workflow whose purpose is test equipment.
- A workflow's T1 proof lives at
  `tests/scenario/workflows/<workflow-id>/{structural.scenario.test.ts,dry-run.scenario.ts}`: exactly
  one collected structural scenario and one sibling live dry-run manifest. The live half may write
  ordinary upstream `run_checkpoints`; its submit-free invariant is zero deltas in
  `write_intents`, `write_attempts`, and `durable_outbox`.
- The dry-run declaration boundary is `src/domain/trust/dry-run-scenario.ts`; the runner/assertions
  are `src/core/dry-run-scenario-runner.ts`, and `src/server/dry-run-scenario/` owns real start-plan,
  start-run, worker-drain, gate-command, receipt, and authority composition. Only `src/cli.ts` may
  dynamically load the non-collected `tests/scenario/**/dry-run.scenario.ts` declaration; no
  production module imports a test module. Blocked targets persist `not-started` before the ready
  runtime factory is called. A ready case declares the receipt service's complete ordered
  `(obligation, authority verdict, mandatory)` tuples, including every `node.*` row; the runner
  compares that list exactly and never projects `absent`/`ambiguous` into a shared verdict.
- **2026-08-30 — deterministic dry-run composition must carry its credential-free gate seam.**
  Fake browser sessions alone do not isolate worker boot from Duo credential identity resolution.
  Composition tests inject the real lease-backed `fixtureDuoCeremonyGates(clock)` through the
  optional `duoCeremony` runtime input and forward it to worker composition. Production CLI callers
  omit that input; absence retains the real production Duo factory and its fail-loud credential
  checks. Never provision operator credentials or replace the real worker drain to make these
  fixture tests pass; preserve their receipt, gate, write-safety, and failure-evidence assertions.
- No default exports.
- A `src/dashboard/surfaces/*.tsx` or `src/dashboard/app/*.tsx` module exports **components only**;
  its hooks, folds, vocabularies and object constants live in a sibling `<surface>-model.ts`
  (`dashboard-refresh-boundary`, ref frontend-backend-integration §8.14, `src/dashboard/AGENTS.md`).
- Archive subviews are dashboard route state (`archiveView`), not `ArchiveWorkspace` local state; a
  cross-takeover door must name the real Archive view in that state rather than open the ledger and
  require a second click.
- **2026-08-25 — dashboard session joins stay authority-shaped (P4).** Group `QueueSurface` rows
  only by their present `session.sessionId`, join a worker only by exact `currentRun.runId`, and retain an
  absent arm's served reason. A pool's declared `desiredWorkers` is distinct from non-terminal
  authority worker-card facts; a missing pool row is no declaration, never a target of one.
- **2026-08-25 — virtual session rows preserve authority across dashboard ticks (P4).** Flatten every
  served member into a fixed layout, mount only the viewport plus bounded overscan, and memoize that
  renderer away from the one-second elapsed-time tick. Give one mounted `listitem` the roving tab stop;
  keyboard moves mount and then focus the designated row. Native scroll owns focus across the whole row
  and its explicitly registered detail portal: focus stays with a descendant while its owner remains
  mounted, then an owned popover closes before an owner leaves the window and the visible roving row takes
  real focus. Unrelated controls stay outside that transfer, and a clamped boundary key clears deferred
  focus before a later resize. Keep clipped values reachable through a detail popover whose invisible
  44px hit area is proven not to overlap another trigger; visual truncation never drops data.
- Kebab-case filenames; `.tsx` only under `src/dashboard/`.
- `verbatimModuleSyntax` + `.js` extensions on relative imports.
- Every durable / wire / config boundary is a recursively strict zod schema; no open records at a
  boundary, no `any`, no unchecked assertion (`strict-boundary-schemas.test.ts`).
- Browser tasks bind the store's exact invariant `DriverDeclaration<ConcreteDriver>` through
  `defineTask(driver, contract, impl)`; never project a semantic driver down to `{system}` or mint a
  second declaration for tasks registered in the same store. Service/workflow tasks remain
  `defineTask(contract, impl)` and receive no driver.
- All time reads go through `src/domain/clock.ts` (`clock-single-source.test.ts`); `manualClock` is
  test-only (`manual-clock-test-only.test.ts`).
- Registry exports are recursively frozen at module load (`src/domain/immutability.ts`).
- Structured errors, never `console.*` in `src/`.
- **2026-08-25 — pool worker identity:** worker composition accepts no default index. The CLI must
  validate an explicit positive `--pool-index`, and `<workflow>-worker-<index>` is the one identity
  shared by the loop, browser-profile partition and authority lease. Never infer an index from
  current pool or lease rows.
- **2026-08-25 — worker process locks observe a fleet; they do not own identity.** Every worker
  start appends its own durable lock record, including restarts. D181 aggregates all records and the
  legacy root lock into one strict restore arm; any live or malformed record refuses restore. Never
  serialize the fleet with a singleton role lock or preempt the authority lease collision. Offline
  restore owns exclusive admission through the authority swap; every runtime acquisition checks
  before and after writing its record and unwinds if restore won. A persisted recovery snapshot is
  evidence, not current liveness or exclusion. Singleton admission must use the atomic filesystem
  claim, never check-then-rename; new ownership records bind PID to OS process birth, and a process
  record may report stopped only after its authority handle closure returned successfully. Reserve
  generation 1 for the observable never-run baseline, so the first acquisition is generation 2;

  intent ids. Never compare global table counts or attribute another run's write to the rehearsal.

  identify a permanent key only by its bounded digest reference; the raw key remains authority-only.

  refusals project only its typed park code instead of replaying that stored free text. A malformed
  staged subject observation names the required canonical format and owning contract, never the
  observed value.

  branches name nodes DOWNSTREAM of their controller — forward references, checked at `build()`

  schema, and a node fragment belongs to the exact frozen step object that created it — equal keys
  are not equal ownership at runtime. Bind that object once per `nodes.ts` with
  `defineWorkflowStepNodeFactory`; define task/transaction/gate fragments and the final category
  through the returned factory rather than repeating the step on every node.
- A contract a descriptor uses but no store implements yet must be listed in
  `config/pending-impl-bindings.json`; the guard fails in both directions (D107).

  before `ctx.driver.commit`. Capture and clock that batch at the call, then deliver commit-role
  span events only after the callback itself settles; winning its deadline race merely requests
  cancellation. The ordinary `withDriver` abort race is not sufficient: the write sequencer must
  cross `withTransactionDriver`'s one-way `retainAfterFence()` boundary immediately after the durable
  fence. Until actual settlement, parent abort and task deadline may request cancellation but must
  not emit, park, return, reset, or close the transaction session. An
  indefinitely non-cooperative callback remains process-owned with an `attempting` intent so
  process-loss recovery, not detached I/O, owns the next action. If task and terminal-span delivery
  both fail, preserve them primary-first in an `AggregateError` and carry it through any parked-write
  cause. Post-click verification starts after authority is fenced, so task lookup, input binding and
  `span.started` emission belong inside the `PostFenceWriteFailure` boundary too; none may escape
  without parking. See ref write-safety §3 and doc 03a §Observed logs.

- **2026-08-30 — a returned artifact URL is consumed only when a mounted browser sink receives it.**
  The Archive route guard drives `ArchivedRunDetail` through Evidence and capture, uses the real
  query/parser, and credits only strict same-pair native `href`/`src` observations. An unused URL
  builder earns nothing. Keep scanner roots, patterns and both-direction pending accounting intact;
  observation failures remain fatal beside orphan-route diagnostics. File-local jsdom proves this
  parent-to-DOM connection, not shell reachability, downloaded bytes, decode or browser geometry.

- **2026-08-30 — an exact resource URL still needs its D183 origin declaration.** Register the
  complete archived-capture wire, not just its unfamiliar paths: UUIDs and state literals are
  closed, while the exact-id URL and fixed availability copy are repository-authored free text.
  Prove that origin through the real archive query and verifier with planted canaries, including
  typed missing/corrupt errors; raw errors alone are normalized before the query and can hide an
  accidental `error.message` substitution. No origin exception or scanner waiver is needed.

- **2026-08-25 — rerun membership is stable-item membership, not row-position equality.** Derive the
  current side again from the immutable intake artifact, durable decisions and their retained
  read instant. `removed` carries the prior manifest row and `added` the current re-derived row,
  keyed only by `itemId`: a mapping that changes identity is remove-plus-add, while one that keeps
  identity uses a separate `changedInputs` vector when its canonical input hash moves. Carry only
  before/after hashes there; the values retain their existing classifications. Missing current
  layout or prior/current row facts must refuse by name; an absent vector is never an empty-vector
  fallback. A reserved manifest id is preflight identity, not proof a manifest exists. Enqueued
  reads bind both terminal projections to their exact committed id; open reads may select only the
  unique latest earlier same-source manifest, never their reservation or a future row. Equal latest
  creation times refuse by session, timestamp and candidate ids rather than selecting by repository
  order. Share the durable
  manifest's field schemas and row refinement with the reviewed wire projection so totals, row
  coverage and stable-item uniqueness cannot drift without broadening data egress.

- **2026-08-25 — an irreversible intake must consume an identity authority reserved before review.**
  Mint `reservedManifestId` in the upload route's durable session write, serve that exact value, and
  make enqueue pass it unchanged into the immutable manifest. Keep terminal `intakeManifestId`
  exclusive to `enqueued` and require equality when a reservation exists. The reservation stays
  optional only for read-forward compatibility; an older row without it refuses by session id and
  must never fall back to a fresh UUID, because that would commit a different plan than the operator
  inspected.

- **2026-08-25 — exact-id readback needs the same identity door at every authority boundary.** A
  repository lookup, recursively strict wire parse, or injected dashboard client can each return a
  valid diagnostic bundle for the wrong id. Compare the requested id to the durable row before
  reading its index or artifacts, compare it again after the wire parse, and keep the requested id
  in the dialog's error state so a foreign response can never rename the selection or its manifest.

- **2026-08-25 — closing an async readback must invalidate its result, not only hide its dialog.**
  Escape can unmount a loading diagnostic-bundle dialog while its durable verification remains in
  flight; an unguarded resolution then remounts the dialog after the operator closed it. Advance a
  request generation on both open and close, and accept a result only for the current generation.
  The manifest fixture must also remain a strict durable `DiagnosticBundle`, distinct from its wire
  projection, or a download test can accidentally prove client reconstruction instead of authority.

- **2026-08-25 — a content-addressed diagnostic row is not evidence of readable bytes.** The D137
  bundle row and attachment index can agree while an artifact has been lost or corrupted; E29 therefore
  re-derives the bundle digest, compares the exact indexed attachments, and drains each content-addressed
  artifact before it serves facts or a manifest. A client-side reconstruction would have made a damaged
  record look download-ready.

- **2026-08-28 — a content-addressed object is not permission to serve it.** The loopback artifact
  route resolves a complete ref only through the diagnostic attachment index, then materializes and
  re-verifies its digest, size and media type before constructing any success response. It and exact-bundle
  readback share one bounded verifier engine while selecting explicit modes: readback drains and hashes
  without retaining chunks, while the byte route copies directly into one exact standalone buffer. Each
  caller retains its own identity/error labels. An uncomposed
  attachment authority is an unavailable capability, not corrupt evidence. A valid id that exists only in
  storage, capture, archive or phone authority is foreign and answers 404; an indexed id whose physical
  object disappeared stays a distinct typed verifier failure and answers a non-retryable 500 here.
  Materialization refuses the first cumulative byte-count crossing before copying that chunk or requesting
  another one. Mutation tests observe the native typed-array copy sink with scoped restoration; iterator
  sentinels cannot prove these invariants because native copies bypass them. Even an unsupported Range is
  refused only after verification, and the capture Host keeps the
  byte route behind the same byte-identical 404 gate as every other operator surface.

- **2026-08-25 — reconnect is not recovery from an unknown event-stream interval.** Bind resume
  evidence to both cursor and projection generation: a cursor from an earlier generation proves
  restart/rebuild, not missed history, and must resnapshot without publishing. Only a same-generation
  historical cursor that retained history cannot replay creates the permanent fact. Its identity is
  the requested cursor plus generation, never the aging reason or moving head; duplicate observation
  leaves the durable row byte-for-byte unchanged. Capture hello and snapshot from one projection
  instant, restart the handshake if publication moves it, and enforce immutability in authority so
  no service, command or direct same-state write can hide or version-bump the fact. All pinned rows
  share the drawer's bounded scroll region with ordinary rows while filters remain reachable.

- **2026-08-25 — exact visual geometry and a usable touch target are separate boxes.** A demo-exact

  semantic button supplies the 44px hit region. Prove the outer points hit that button and that its
  effective rectangle intersects no neighboring control; increasing the shared button size would
  silently change every header's fidelity instead.

  span supplies its exact `(nodeId, taskId)` and redacted page point; the module/store binding supplies
  a browser system only when that exact origin declares one. The Logs query resolves exactly one
  root-composed data origin for the pair and refuses missing or ambiguous origins by file and line;
  one service origin with no browser system stays absent on wire and screen. Defaulting to `read` or
  a plausible system turns a trustworthy observation into an attributed lie. Observed/fenced span rows are indexed by the
  disk-tail projector at append time; the GET never re-derives their partitions from record-time run
  instants. A continuation cursor binds an immutable combined snapshot, so a later backdated append is
  visible on a fresh first page and cannot duplicate or displace rows in an existing page walk.

- **2026-08-25 — a parity fixture must contain the state it claims to prove.** The ordinary Start
  Run fixture truthfully covered Person Lookup's input/plan flow, but that meant it could not see the

  profile for the registry shape under review; a broad fixture that redraws unrelated references hides

  workflow through the real interpreter, beat-⑦ checkpoint read-back, terminal authority and
  receipt derivation. A `walkDescriptor` assertion proves binds and derive shape, but it cannot
  prove that any durable row was read or that a run terminalized from it.

- **2026-08-25 — a preview has to be asserted in the receipt's real vocabulary.** A dry-run
  transaction stores no transaction checkpoint, so Kuali finalization receipts derive four
  cross-source obligations as `unknown` and the literal reload-read-back obligation as `absent`;

  node row, or claiming partial confidence makes the manifest lie about authority. Compare the
  whole ordered tuple list. Likewise, `replay: "always-rerun"` forbids reuse but still writes the

  durable failure before a `transaction.previewed` event exists. Malformed subject text looked
  useful in a format error, but that message fans out to failure, receipt, span and log sinks; keep
  the contract/format actionable and omit the observed text entirely.

- **2026-08-25 — retiring a proof workflow does not retire the real workflow's vocabulary.** The
  timekeeper annotation staging/read-back schemas and tasks belonged only to D266's dismantled test

  separation finalization. Audit every deleted contract through driver, fake, receipt and catalog
  dependents; preserve shared semantic elements under the real task that still consumes them.

- **2026-08-25 — Dry-run evidence must model pre-browser blockage explicitly.** A gone subject has
  no run or trace identity to record, so nullable identities invite fabrication; use the strict
  `not-started` blocked arm. Keep assertion diagnostics to safe reason slugs: free text can leak the
  resolved subject value into otherwise label-only evidence.

- **2026-08-25 — Write-safety tables do not share one run key.** `write_intents` carries the run id,

  count looked like a delta but could blame concurrent work on the rehearsal; derive all three
  counts from the named run's intent set, before and after, and assert the exact zero tuple.

## After changes

Run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test:coverage` before committing (D191 —
`test:coverage` REPLACES the earlier `test` + `test:architecture` pair as the per-commit gate; both
scripts stay available for a targeted run). Add a new guard file **and** its
`docs/rebuild/guard-inventory.json` entry in the same commit — `guard-manifest.test.ts` checks both
directions. Retiring a guard requires an explicit `retired` entry naming the deciding decision and
where the invariant went; a guard that simply disappears is indistinguishable from an accident.

Never push to any remote without explicit instruction.

**What this doc is.** The contract for everything the operator SEES and for every mechanism that
feeds it: the span/notes event model (§1), the storage and transport split between authority and
projection (§2), the descriptor fields this layer consumes (§3), the completion contract (§4), the
cross-repo runtime boundary (§5), and one section per operator surface (§9). It is a REFERENCE
spec — cited as `ref dashboard-surfaces §N` and never actionable on its own. What is scheduled, and
what is left, lives in the phase docs `docs/rebuild/00`–`05` and in `docs/roadmap/roadmap.md`.

descriptor surface. §4–§5 are two contracts this doc contributed and another doc consumes. §6 is
the rot table, §7 the worked example, §8 the settled questions. §9 is the operator surfaces, one
numbered subsection per **wire square**.

### 1.1 Primitives

Everything observable is one append-only stream of **span events**. Four span kinds live in
`spans/` (worker / browser / run / task) plus gate events and the dry-run preview; **per-action
attribution rides the notes stream** (D10) — an action is a note addressed to its owning task span,
not a span of its own. That keeps the span stream small enough to be the queue/timeline truth while
preserving per-action drill-down. The notes half of that sentence is a CONTRACT and not yet a fact:
see *The notes stream* at the end of this section.

```
worker ──┬─ browser / auth / idle …        (daemon process lifetime; replaces sessions/*)
         │
run ─────┬─ task                           (one descriptor node — ref workflow-model's task chain)
         ├─ task …
         ├─ gate events                    (parked-on-operator/system states, D5)
         └─ transaction.previewed          (a dry run's transaction node — D210)
                └─ actions → notes stream  (click/fill/goto/ocr-page/… — addressed by spanPath;
                                            DECLARED, no production emitter today)
```

**Identity.** A run or task span is `(runId, attempt, spanPath)`; a worker or browser span is
`(workerId, spanPath)` — workers persist across runs, so they never receive a synthetic run id.
"Opened and closed exactly once" holds per identity, and the JSONL writer enforces it at emit
(`createSpanJsonlWriter`): a second `run.queued` for one identity throws, so does re-opening or
re-ending a span this process already opened or ended. A close with no locally-seen open is allowed
on purpose — a restart may legitimately end a span an earlier process opened, and refusing it would
make every recovery emit path throw.

The path grammar is `ref workflow-model` §6's, imported rather than redefined, and composed by
`src/core/span-emitter.ts` so no caller spells one:

```
run span:      sp-080639-0041                            the frozen trace id itself
task span:     sp-080639-0041/timecard-search#2.1        <trace>/<nodeId>#<claimGeneration>.<taskAttempt>
worker span:   worker/separations/worker-1
browser span:  worker/separations/worker-1/browser:ucpath#<sessionId>
```

**`#<claimGeneration>.<taskAttempt>` is D214's fix and it is load-bearing.** A gate park and its
resume are two claims inside ONE attempt, and an `always-rerun` node re-executes across that
boundary by design — before D214 both executions emitted the same path, so the projector's
`(runId, attempt, spanPath)` fold and the timeline's React seed each collapsed two genuinely
different executions into one (D123's lesson, one level in). Every reader still parses the node id
as everything before the LAST `#`, so a stored pre-D214 stream stays readable.

**The union is thirteen strict arms** (`SpanEventWireSchema`, `src/events/types.ts`). Every arm
carries `t`, `ts`, `workflow` and `pid` plus its identity tuple; `t` alone cannot discriminate,
because `span.started`/`span.ended` legitimately appear for four kinds, so the union is plain and
each arm is a `strictObject`.

| arm | identity | what it adds | emitted by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run.queued` | run | the row's write-once identity: `itemId`, `parentRunId?`, `shape`, `priority`, `dryRun`, `retryOf?`, `actorId`, `title`, `subtitle?`, `descriptorVersion`, `contractFingerprint`, `resolvedInstance`, `configFingerprint`, `configSnapshotId` | the BFF command service, on an applied `start-run`, intake enqueue or `retry` |
| `run.claimed` | run | `workerId` | the executor |
| `run.requeued` | run | `cause` (`reassign` · `bump` · `recovery` · `provider-capacity`), `nextAttempt` | the executor |
| `span.started` `kind:"task"` | run | `name` (the node's LABEL), `system?` | the executor |
| `span.started` `kind:"worker"\|"browser"` | worker | `name`, `system?` | the worker composition |
| `gate.opened` | run | `gate` | the executor |
| `gate.resolved` | run | `gate`, `resolutionKey`, `resultHash` | the BFF command service, on an applied `resolve-gate` |
| `transaction.previewed` | run | `node`, `subject` (`match` · `mismatch` · `unscoped` · `not-observed`), `externalCommit: "none"` | the executor, on a dry run's transaction node (D210/D215) |
| `transaction.fenced` | run | `node`, `taskId` | the write sequencer, after the commit callback settles; `ts` remains the durable fence instant |
| `data.observed` | run | `nodeId`, `taskId`, `observedAt`, `points` — one entry per recorded point: `direction`, `field`, and its value split into evidence LEAVES, each already redacted | the executor, once per `ctx.recordData` call (D270) |
| `span.ended` `kind:"task"` | run | `outcome`, `failureId?`, `errorSummary?`, `notRunReason?` | the executor |
| `span.ended` `kind:"run"` | run | `outcome`, `failureId?` | the executor |
| `span.ended` `kind:"worker"\|"browser"` | worker | `outcome`, `errorSummary?` | the worker composition |

`outcome` is `done · failed · cancelled · discarded · skipped · interrupted · superseded` —
**cancelled, discarded, interrupted and superseded are first-class outcomes**, and the
`failed + step:"cancelled"` sentinel family the legacy tree needs does not exist here. `skipped` is
a task outcome, and `notRunReason` (`condition-false` · `branch-not-selected`) may appear only on
it — a refinement enforces that, because a `done` span carrying a not-run reason would describe two
different things at once. Its ABSENCE means "no reason was recorded" and must stay legible as
that; it is never back-filled with a plausible one (D123).

**The kernel's port is eleven of those arms, not thirteen.** `ExecutorSpanEventSchema`
(`src/core/span-emitter.ts`) is the executor's REQUIRED sink — no default, no no-op — and it
deliberately omits `run.queued` and `gate.resolved`, which the BFF emits because it is where the
enqueue and the gate resolution are applied. The two schemas are parity twins over the arms they
share, and the twin-ness is not free: D215's fourth `transaction.previewed` verdict landed in the
kernel's union and never reached this wire leaf, so the FIRST preview that ever settled threw
inside the JSONL writer and killed a live worker one emit short of its terminal (separations
§9.15). The pinning cases are `tests/unit/events/span-events.test.ts`, and the lesson they now
carry is to enumerate the VALUES a producer can emit rather than sampling the shapes.

**`data.observed` is the OBSERVED LOG, and it is an emission rather than a scrape (D270).** Every
point a task records through `ctx.recordData` — the D115 collector — is what the run actually READ
or WROTE in the system's own words, and until D270 those points validated the output and were then
discarded. They now ride this arm, on the producing task's own span path, one event per
`recordData` CALL: a batch is one observation of the page, so the collector reads the clock once per
call and the event's `observedAt` is that single instant rather than one derived from whichever
point happened to be first. Probe, prepare and verify deliver that event synchronously. Commit
freezes the same call-time batch but delays redaction and delivery until its callback settles; this
one delivery exception keeps the fallible span sink outside the durable fence→external-click
window without changing the evidence instant.

Four properties are worth stating where a reader meets the arm.

- **Record time, not finalization.** Every call is validated and stamped immediately. Probe,
  prepare and verify emit immediately, so a later throw cannot erase the observation. Commit
  batches flush after callback settlement even when that callback throws; their `observedAt`
  remains the call instant, not the flush instant.
- **Redacted by DECLARATION, per leaf.** Each point's value is split by the provenance collector's
  own leaf rule and pushed through `redactEvidenceLeaf` — the same declared table
  (`ref operator-trust` §2.3) the D82 receipt uses, never a second implementation. An UNDECLARED
  leaf fails the recording task by name; on commit, that post-callback refusal parks the fenced
  write. Dropping it would make a log look complete while hiding what the run read.
- **`direction` is carried natively, `system` is NOT.** `DataPoint` has always carried read/write,
  which the Context rail has to DERIVE from the producing node's declared task-contract `effect`
  because the checkpoint row has no such field (D252) — so an observed log is strictly better placed
  than the rail to say what the run did to the world and must not re-derive what it holds. The
  system is declared by the STORE implementing the task and reaches the wire through
  `RunDetailDescriptorView.dataOrigins`, composed at the root because a descriptor may not reach a
  store (D106); a `system` field here would be a second authority over a fact the declaration
  already owns.
- **The queue projection ignores it BY NAME.** The queue row's vocabulary is task spans and terminal
  outcomes, and folding a page observation into a span it is not would be D123's collapse again — so
  the arm is refused a fold explicitly, which is what keeps a stream carrying it from degrading
  `ingestFromDisk` and triggering the guarded rebuild (D218). Rendering the rows is `03a` §Observed
  logs' FE row. `transaction.fenced` is ignored by the queue projection by name for the same reason.

It rides `spans/` and adds no file kind: §2.1's layout is unchanged, and no note is written, so
`assertNoteWithinRunScope` is not on this path at all.

**What the wire deliberately does NOT carry.** Each of these is a named absence, not an oversight,
and every one of them was in an earlier draft of this section:

- **`span.patched`** — RETIRED by D254; see the block below.
- **`subject.observed`** — recorded at `src/events/types.ts:30` as a deliberate absence. Subject
  comparison is the write sequencer's beat ③ and lands in the durable intent and its binding proof
  (`ref write-safety` §5), not on a display stream.
- **`verdict` on `span.ended`** — there is no such field, so the descriptor's `verdicts` vocabulary
  (§3.2) has nothing to key off. It is declared, validated at `build()` and SERVED to the Workflow
  Explorer as declared prose (`src/server/dashboard/queries/explorer.ts`), and no status is derived
  from it anywhere. §1.3 is where that promise was made; this is where it is unmet.
- **`evidenceReceiptId` on `span.ended`** — the receipt is DERIVED from authority (D82/D141) and
  looked up by `runId`; carrying its id on a display event would put a second, staler pointer beside
  the one the surfaces already resolve.
- **`resultRef` on `gate.resolved`** — a gate result is keyed by `(runId, gateId)` in authority, so
  a separate ref id would duplicate an identity that already exists. `resultHash` stays, because a
  digest is a fact about the bytes rather than a second address.
- **`subject`, `subjectKind`, `input`/`sensitiveInputRef` and `displayOnly` on `run.queued`** — the
  KIND axis, the run's business input and the task-less display row were all in the 1g draft and
  none of them is on the wire. The input lives in the immutable run envelope in authority; the
  subject reaches the queue as the projection's `title`, replaced once from the descriptor's own
  `subjectProjection` leaf when the run's reads settle it (§1.2); and no enqueue path in `src/` can
  produce a `displayOnly` row, because none can produce the `operation` shape it belongs to (§1.3).

The wire schemas are the contract; TypeScript declarations are readable views of them.
`SpanEventWireSchema`, `NoteWireSchema`, every `*WireSchema` and the SSE payload schemas are strict
zod unions whose inferred types ARE the implementation types. Native JSONL read, SQLite read/write,
HTTP input/output, SSE emission and fixture load all parse at the boundary. Unknown keys, invalid
ISO instants, unbranded ids, non-canonical JSON, `NaN` and invalid state combinations fail — they
are never cast into the model. An optional offline historical importer owns its own explicit-version
parse and visible quarantine contract; it is not a runtime boundary.

#### D254 — the `span.patched` detail channel is RETIRED (2026-08-20, operator ruling)

<!-- roadmap: track-b -->

**`span.patched` is removed from the span vocabulary.** It carried a declared per-workflow key set
(`descriptor.details`) and folded into a `row.details` map the run-detail Context rail read. It had
**zero production emitters, in the strongest available sense**: the kernel's `SpanEmitter` port
(`src/core/span-emitter.ts`) never carried the arm, so no code path in `src/` could produce one; the
only producers that ever existed were test fixtures; and `.tracker-rebuild/spans` — every real run
this program has ever executed — holds no such line. Every surface fed by the channel therefore
rendered its empty state permanently, through every green gate, since 1g-spine. The gap was recorded
in `docs/findings/dashboard-projection.md` on 2026-08-14 (found while building the subject title,
which reads a CHECKPOINT for exactly this reason — §1.2 above).

**The ruling is to remove, not to build.** An arm nothing can emit is not "unused", it is
unreachable, and leaving a declared vocabulary arm in place makes the wire claim a capability the
runtime does not have. Retiring is reversible and honest; building the emitter is work nobody asked
for. What was removed, end to end:

| Site | What went |
|---|---|
| `src/events/types.ts` | the `SpanPatchedSchema` arm, `DetailUpdateWireSchema`, its key schema, `SPAN_IDENTITY_ATTRIBUTE_KEYS` (whose only reader was the patch key refusal), and the now-unused JSON value schema |
| `src/infra/events/span-jsonl-writer.ts` | the declared-key enforcement branch and the `declaredDetails` dep it needed — a `span.patched` line now fails `SpanEventWireSchema.parse` before any byte reaches disk |
| `src/server/dashboard/compose.ts`, `src/server/worker/compose.ts` | the two `declaredDetails` injections |
| `src/server/dashboard/projectors/run-queue-projection.ts` | the fold arm and the `details` field of `RunFoldRecord` (a rebuildable projection — the fold schema hash moves and the tail re-folds from disk; nothing durable holds this shape) |
| `src/server/dashboard/queries/run-detail.ts` | the `row.details` loop in the Context-rail payload, the `details` member of `RunDetailDescriptorView`, and `editableEntryOf`'s `display` argument and checkpoint-less arm |

**`descriptor.details` STAYS, with its meaning restated.** It is no longer a patch-key vocabulary; it
is a DECLARATION with three real readers — the evidence receipt's mandatory-leaf set
(`src/core/evidence-receipt.ts`), the run-detail data-origin bound (`dataOriginViewsOf`, whose
resolved path set is `details[].source` ∪ `capabilities.editData.fields`), and the Explorer's field
census. Removing it would have been the over-correction: three live consumers, one dead one.

**What the Context rail lists is now exactly one rule.** A row exists iff a `capabilities.editData`
field has a stored checkpoint — D252's "the Data section lists values the run TOUCHED", made
structural rather than defended by a guard clause. Two consequences are deliberate. A declared
`details` spec that is not a correctable field contributes NO row (before this it contributed one
only in a fixture); and `editableEntryOf` takes the checkpoint as a parameter, so "there is a stored
checkpoint" is stated in the type instead of re-derived and re-answered.

**The named alternative, and why it was not taken.** Declared details could be served from
checkpoints the way D252 serves correctable fields — the same `latestCheckpoint` read is one line
away. That is a BUILD (it decides which declared leaves belong on an operator surface, their order
and their labels), and the surface's membership was decided by D252 two days earlier. **The trigger
that re-opens it:** an operator asking for a declared, non-correctable value on the run-detail rail.
The answer then is a checkpoint read, never a re-added event arm — the channel's defect was never its
shape, it was that nothing wrote it.

**Reading a historical line.** A `span.patched` line would now be refused BY NAME by the tail, which
degrades the projection and schedules the guarded rebuild (D218). That is the correct answer and
costs nothing, because no such line exists: the retirement was verified against the real state root,
not merely against the source tree.

**The notes stream — declared, composed, and written by nothing.** Notes are the high-volume half
of D10: log lines, screenshots, per-action records, data points. They carry the same `SpanRef`
addressing as spans, so a note attributes to its exact task attempt or worker lifetime:

```ts
// src/events/types.ts — NoteWireSchema, a union over the two identity tuples
{ ...identity, ts, workflow, pid,
  level: "step" | "success" | "error" | "waiting" | "warn" | "debug",
  message: string,
  fields?: readonly NoteFieldWire[],   // closed kind union: text | count | digest | last4 | basename
}
```

`fields` is a closed key/value union whose kinds mirror the redaction transforms (`ref
clock-config-secrets`): a value that reached this wire either passed `allow` as text or was
transformed, and a dropped field does not appear at all. Notes are evidence, not control state — a
new structured field is a schema extension, high-cardinality exploratory metadata belongs in a
schema-versioned diagnostic attachment, and no projector, command handler, retry policy or workflow
bind may branch on note prose or an untyped attachment payload.

**Nothing writes it.** `emitNote` exists and is the only entry
(`src/infra/events/note-jsonl-writer.ts`); the writer is constructed in the dashboard composition
and exposed on its handle (`src/server/dashboard/compose.ts`) — and **no caller in `src/` ever
invokes it.** The only callers are test and fixture files. The worker, which is where a run's log
lines would come from, writes structured JSON to stdout instead (`lineTaskLogger`,
`src/server/worker/compose.ts`). At D254's own evidentiary bar — verified against the real state
root, not merely against the source tree — **`.tracker-rebuild/notes/` does not exist**: the state
root holds a `spans/` directory with a file per workflow-day and no notes directory at all.

Three consequences are worth stating where a reader meets them, because each reads as a rendering
quirk from the surface side. The run-detail **Logs** section re-reads that stream per request
(`noteLinesForRun`, `src/server/dashboard/queries/run-detail.ts`) and therefore serves an empty
page. `defaultTabFor` opens a **failed** run on Logs (`log-panel-model.ts`), so the default tab for
the one run an operator most needs to read is the empty one. And the `notes/` line in the §2.1
layout, the "second grep" rationale there, and §1.2's *timeline ← notes* row all describe a stream
with no producer.

This is `span.patched`'s shape one stream over — machinery whose consumers are complete and whose
producer was never written — with two differences that decide the disposition. The channel is
REACHABLE (a call to `emitNote` writes a line and the Logs section reads it back), and it has a
named owner: `{#observed-logs}` in the tree, whose whole premise is that the log carries the facts
each task recorded. So this is a to-build, not a retirement.

The declared attribution fields the 1g draft named on the note — `action` (task + semantic UI id +
page-state transition) and `attachment` (screenshot / data point / diagnostic) — are not on
`NoteWireSchema` either, and are recorded as the driver-instrumentation slice's, at
`src/events/types.ts:30`.

**Volume, the reason for the split.** The legacy per-page OCR pipeline emits zero tracker rows —
its state rides ~8–12 deduped, 250 ms-debounced row snapshots per run. A naive per-action SPAN
stream would multiply that by orders of magnitude. Under D10 the split is: `spans/` carries run,
task, gate and preview events — roughly **10–40 events per run**, bounded by the descriptor's node
count × attempts and not by page or click counts — and everything per-action lands in `notes/` at
roughly today's log-line volume (hundreds per OCR run). Queue and timeline projections read spans
only; notes load lazily per selected run. That bound is what makes the span stream safe to fold on
every tick, and it holds today because the span half is real.

### 1.3 Decision: archetypes survive as vocabulary, die as per-row stamps

The four row shapes (`single | preview | operation | operation-member`) are **kept** — they are the
proven queue vocabulary — and the mechanism that replaced re-stamping is as-built:

- **Declared on the descriptor** (`surface.shape` or `surface.resolveShape: "by-input"`) and
  materialized **once** on `run.queued.shape`. A member's shape is set by the fan-out dispatcher on
  the child's own `run.queued`.
- **Never re-stamped, structurally.** `run.queued` is the only arm of the union that names an
  identity attribute; every other arm is a `strictObject` that does not, so a re-stamp does not
  parse. The whole legacy re-stamp bug class is unrepresentable rather than merely banned.
- **No legacy normalization** (`batch` → `operation`) in this runtime. An optional versioned
  one-time historical import would own that translation (§5).

Two of the three axes did not survive as stamps, and the doc said otherwise until 2026-08-20.

**The KIND axis is not on the wire.** `subjectKind` appears nowhere in `src/`. What a run is ABOUT
reaches the operator as the projection's `title` — composed by the descriptor's `presentation.title`
from the start input and REPLACED once, when the run's own reads settle the subject at the leaf the
descriptor declares (`subjectProjection`) — and as `panelKind` for layout. Kind-dispatched titling
survived; a per-row kind stamp did not, and nothing needed one.

**Three of the four shapes have no producer.** Every enqueue path in `src/` stamps
`shape: "single"` — `command-kernel.ts:1617` and `:2274`, `capture-intake-handoff.ts:242`,
`services/start/plan.ts` — and every registered descriptor declares `surface: { shape: "single" }`.
The kernel says so itself at `command-kernel.ts:1613-1616`: *"the coordinator/member fan-out has no
runtime yet (nothing mints an `operation` run)"*. The projection, the containment fold,
`memberRollup`, `memberPreview`, the member well and the `run-group`/`run-member` parity references
are all real and all fed by hand-composed fixtures. Building the presentation ahead of the workflow
is correct — §4's completion contract is what will mint these rows, at order 4 — but the doc must
say it is ahead, and §9's group-row decisions must be read as a contract for a shape the system
cannot yet create.

Derived statuses stop being per-workflow code where a universal mechanism exists — one of the two
promised here is built and one is not:

- **An open operator gate is a universal projection rule**, not a per-workflow predicate: a run with
  an open gate row projects `awaiting-approval` and the queue draws it with the gate's own age
  (D12). OCR would only have to declare the gate.
- **Descriptor-declared verdict mappings are NOT wired.** `verdicts` is authored as plain data,
  validated at `build()` (`assertUnique` over the keys, `src/base/workflow.ts`) and served to the
  Workflow Explorer as declared prose — and the thing it was to be keyed off,
  `span.ended.verdict`, does not exist (§1.1). So person-lookup's `notFound` is not rendered from a
  verdict today. What this section DID buy is the deletion it promised: there is no
  `statusExtensions` function registry, and no surface may branch on a workflow id
  (`dashboard-wire-boundary`'s *branches on no concrete workflow id* arm). The vocabulary is data;
  the channel that would carry a value is the open half.

The rebuild owns the distinct `.tracker-rebuild/` state root. Production `src` owns `.tracker/`;
neither runtime reads or writes the other's root.

```
.tracker-rebuild/
├── spans/   <workflow>-<date>.jsonl   span events (low volume — the queue/timeline truth)
├── notes/   <workflow>-<date>.jsonl   notes (high volume — logs, actions, screenshots, data points)
│                                      DECLARED, never written — the directory does not exist (§1.1)
├── evidence/<runId>/                  run receipts + redacted diagnostic bundle manifests (ref operator-trust)
├── artifacts/<hash>.artifact          content-addressed task outputs; atomic, immutable bytes
├── ledger/  <system>-<date>.jsonl     immutable write receipts (D21; shape owned by ref write-safety §6) —
│                                      ordered, actor-attributed, append-only, per-SYSTEM+day,
│                                      NEVER pruned (the audit floor; hash chain deferred by D79)
├── backups/state/                     checksummed online backups + restore manifests (§2.5)
└── state.db                           SQLite — claims/checkpoints/intents/outboxes,

                                       read projections alone are rebuildable
```

**Which of these the runtime actually writes.** `spans/`, `artifacts/`, `backups/`, `locks/` (D181)
and `state.db` are created and written today. Three are not, each for its own reason and each
verified against the real state root rather than against the source tree:

- **`notes/`** — nothing calls `emitNote`, so the directory has never existed (§1.1).
- **`ledger/`** — the projector is written and unit-proven (`src/infra/ledger/ledger-projector.ts`,
  D134's five ordered durable facts, guarded by `ledger-projector`) and **`createLedgerProjector` has no production caller**: its
  only callers are tests. Beat ⑦ does write the durable ledger OUTBOX row inside its authority
  transaction (`ref write-safety` §5), which is the fact the audit floor depends on — nothing
  drains it to a file. The READ half is composed and live (`createLedgerReadThrough`, shared by the
  archive's line pointers and D236's Activity block), so both read a corpus that is currently
  empty. This is §1.1's notes gap a second time: a complete mechanism whose producer was never
  wired. It is not a retirement candidate — a real HR write's immutable receipt is the audit floor
  D21 exists for, and the outbox rows that feed it are already durable.
- **`evidence/<runId>/`** — the receipt moved into authority. D82's `RunEvidenceReceipt` is DERIVED
  from authority and stored as a durable row (`src/core/evidence-receipt.ts`, D141), not as a file,
  and the diagnostic bundle's attachments live in the content-addressed `artifacts/` store by
  digest (D137). What this layout line describes is a path shape nothing writes; what it means —
  evidence is indexed by content hash and missing capture is recorded explicitly — is as-built one
  layer over, in SQLite.

Rationale against alternatives:
- **Why not SQLite-only?** The operator greps files. **The design is two greps:**
  `grep sp-080639 .tracker-rebuild/spans/*.jsonl` answers *what happened* (state transitions,
  outcomes, gates), and `grep sp-080639 .tracker-rebuild/notes/*.jsonl` was to answer *what it did*
  (log lines, per-action records, screenshots) — one trace id returning the whole operation tree
  across workflows in both. **Only the first grep answers anything today**, and the cost is not the
  one this bullet used to record: the `spans/` grep does not contain log-line text (that is the real
  D10 split cost, as documented) AND the second grep has no file to read. `{#observed-logs}` owns
  closing it.
- **Why split spans/notes?** Queue and timeline projections read spans only (§1.1's volume note);
  notes load lazily per selected run. Mirrors the legacy rows/logs split, which was proven.
- **Why a separate `ledger/` (D21 — owner = this doc)?** Ref write-safety's write-safety layer files one
  immutable receipt per real HR mutation (the projector that appends it is unwired — see above). It is partitioned per-**system**+day so
  `grep 10001573 .tracker-rebuild/ledger/ucpath-*.jsonl` answers "what did we file for this person,
  across time." It is ordered, actor-attributed, and **never pruned**. Ref write-safety owns
  the entry *shape* (`LedgerEntry`, §6 there); this doc owns that the dir lives in the layout and is
  exempt from `clean-tracker`.
- **Base retention — DECIDED (D86):** `notes/` and `spans/` both prune at **30 days**.
  `ledger/` is exempt from both — its never-pruned floor now sits **above a settled number, not a
  guess** (this is what ref write-safety §6 references). Legacy `.tracker/` retention is unchanged and owned
  only by production `src`.
- **Why per-workflow files?** Small greppable files; partition key matches the SSE topic scope.
  Worker spans write to their workflow's file (a daemon serves one workflow).
- **Span/note write discipline (ported):** append-at-now partitioning; cross-midnight solved at the
  read layer with the OPEN-span forward-merge (same algorithm as `cross-midnight.ts`); synchronous
  SIGINT terminal writes; `O_APPEND` single-line writes. **Ledger is different:** executors write
  durable outbox rows and one serialized projector assigns ordered sequence and appends (ref write-safety).
- **A note addressed to a run is written only inside that run's partition scope.** Append-at-now
  partitioning and a scoped reader are two clocks with nothing between them: the writer files a line
  under `localDatePart(clock.now())`, and a logs GET opens only the `(workflow, date)` partitions a
  run's own durable instants select. So the scope is ONE shared function —
  `runNotePartitionScope` in `src/domain/run/note-scope.ts` — a producer ASSERTS against
  before the append (`assertNoteWithinRunScope`, refusing by name and naming the run, the note's
  instant, its partition day and the bounds), and the logs reader opens exactly those partitions.
  The producer's window is composed from authority alone and the reader's from authority PLUS the
  span fold, so the reader's instant set is a superset and its window contains the producer's by
  construction: a note the assertion admits is a note the reader opens the partition for. The
  margin is asymmetric — none below (a note cannot predate its run's enqueue) and ONE day above (the
  midnight a worker's last note can fall the other side of from the transition that closed the run).
  `{#observed-logs}`, the first production note producer, inherits this rule: a note filed outside
  the scope is a line on disk that the run's own logs tab can never serve, which is a silent drop.
- **Local artifacts are not hidden task writes (D45).** A read task may create only immutable,
  content-addressed bytes under `artifacts/` through ref task-contract's writer; the returned `{id,sha256,bytes,
  mediaType}` is canonical JSON and checkpoints reference it without exposing a filesystem path.
  Per D97, `id` remains the existing UUID-backed `ArtifactId`; `sha256` is the distinct content
  identity and private `artifacts/<hash>.artifact` key. Byte-identical puts are idempotent and
  return the same public reference. The backing path is never part of a task, checkpoint, or wire
  contract.
  Mutable operator artifacts (for
  example i9's retention workbook) are different: the node checkpoint and a stable-keyed
  `artifact_outbox` row commit atomically in SQLite, then a single sink projector performs
  temp+fsync+atomic-replace and records the projected content hash. Duplicate outboxes/key retries
  are no-ops. A blocking projection failure parks the run; it never reports done while silently
  dropping the workbook update.
- **Evidence is indexed, not scattered.** `evidence/<runId>/receipt.json` points to immutable
  screenshots/artifacts/failures by content hash and records missing capture explicitly. Diagnostic
  bundles redact by schema before writing; they never copy `.env`, cookies, browser storage, raw
  SSNs, or unrestricted input blobs (ref operator-trust §3).

tokens fail with a conflict and trigger a fresh projection.

Per-run detail (timeline, sections) stays request/response plus a per-run SSE topic, and the
payload is already merged and ordered server-side — no client owns merge or dedup heuristics.

### 2.3 SQLite (role per D14)

<!-- roadmap: p1-authority -->

_Its checklist is the `p1-authority` status block under §2 — one block per node per doc._

`state.db` has **two classes of table with different authority**:

- **System-of-record (NOT rebuildable and never deleted by projection/runtime row maintenance):**
  the task/claim store (tasks, leases,
  dependencies, delegation manifests, commands, start plans, terminal authorizations/results, failures,
  notifications, capture sessions/photo order/finalization outboxes — ref workflow-model §5.7's checkpoint payloads,
  §4.4's `ocr_approvals` manifests, and
  ref write-safety's permanent-key `write_intents`, `write_attempts`, and durable outbox, plus
  stable-keyed local `artifact_outbox`/sink-head rows). The system-of-record set is
  "planned/accepted run authority + claims + checkpoint/result/failure payloads + write
  authority/outboxes + local artifact projection authority + in-progress capture/handoff
  authority." Losing any of these loses accepted input, claims, resumable/terminal results,
  structured failure truth, in-flight write fences, or accepted capture work — they have no JSONL
  double.
- **Projection tables (rebuildable):** span-shaped read models (`spans`, `gates`, `notes`,
  `runs_view`) fed by one projector consuming only native rebuild spans — **FROM DISK,
  cross-process (D218)**: the worker emits its task spans from a separate OS process, so the
  projector's one live feed is an offset-aware tail of the stream files, never an in-process emit
  hook. These — and only these — can be deleted and rebuilt from JSONL, with today's operational
  rules: JSONL writes first, projection applies after (structural under D218 — the fold can only
  see bytes already landed), projection failures schedule guarded rebuilds and never block
  workflows; source identity is `resolve(path)`; deletion tombstones and offline compaction port
  as-is.

The system-of-record class includes a singleton `authority_meta(schema_version,
authority_generation,updated_at)`. The infra adapter exposes separate authority and projection
transaction APIs; repositories cannot execute arbitrary SQL or receive the raw connection. Every
top-level committed transaction that mutates at least one authority table increments
`authority_generation` exactly once inside that same transaction; projection-only rebuilds do not.
Nested authority operations share the outer transaction/generation increment. The table-class
registry generates coverage tests that mutate each authority repository and prove the generation
advances, then mutate each projection repository and prove it does not. A newly added authority
table without a registered mutator test fails. This makes D72 backup RPO comparison an actual
monotonic authority fact rather than a timestamp guess.
